newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French 10-year bond futures closed lower on consolidation in a market which, failing to find direction in Europe, focused on nervousness in the U.S. market.

"We are in typical consolidation, looking for direction. In the absence of anything new in Europe, we are looking at the United States, which is pretty nervous," one dealer said. "The underlying upward trend is not at risk, but it will take a bit of time to start climbing again, depending on a status quo on rates by the Federal Reserve or a poor German indicator."
In the meantime he expected the 10-year futures contract to remain stuck between 130.70 and 130.06, or even 129.50.

The contract reached its day's high of 130.46 on news of an unexpected fall in durable goods orders in the United States in December, but then dropped sharply to a low of 130.00 as U.S. Treasury bonds erased gains made on the U.S. data.

Dealers said markets were now awaiting U.S. fourth quarter gross domestic product data due on Friday, on hopes it would confirm expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would hold rates unchanged at its next meeting on Febuary 4 and 5.

"Basically the trend is upwards, and the flattening in the curve seen for some time looks set to continue," one dealer said. "Nothing has changed, the fall in German and French (official) rates which everyone was waiting for will no doubt happen a bit later due to the rise in the dollar," he said.
A Reuter poll conducted on Tuesday showed economists expect the Bank of France to hold rates unchanged after the fortnightly meeting of its monetary policy council on Thursday.
They said the rise in the dollar had taken the pressure off the central bank to lower rates.
